> Someone has to make an effort at reconciliation if these conflicts are ever going to end. 
 
In this release, we finally fix the odd number of CPU cores bug, pave the way for lighter weight challenges, make Anubis more adaptable, and more. 
 
### Big ticket items 
 
#### Proof of React challenge 
 
A new "proof of React" has been added. It runs a simple app in React that has several chained hooks. It is much more lightweight than the proof of work check. 
 
#### Smaller features 
 
- The `segments` function was added for splitting a path into its slash-separated segments. 
- Added possibility to disable HTTP keep-alive to support backends not properly handling it. 
- When issuing a challenge, Anubis stores information about that challenge into the store. That stored information is later used to validate challenge responses. This works around nondeterminism in bot rules. (#917) 
- One of the biggest sources of lag in Firefox has been eliminated: the use of WebCrypto. Now whenever Anubis detects the client is using Firefox (or Pale Moon), it will swap over to a pure-JS implementation of SHA-256 for speed. 
- Proof of work solving has had a complete overhaul and rethink based on feedback from browser engine developers, frontend experts, and overall performance profiling. 
- Optimize the performance of the pure-JS Anubis solver. 
- Web Workers are stored as dedicated JavaScript files in `static/js/workers/*.mjs`. 
- Pave the way for non-SHA256 solver methods and eventually one that uses WebAssembly (or WebAssembly code compiled to JS for those that disable WebAssembly). 
- Legacy JavaScript code has been eliminated. 
- When parsing Open Graph tags, add any URLs found in the responses to a temporary "allow cache" so that social preview images work. 
- The hard dependency on WebCrypto has been removed, allowing a proof of work challenge to work over plain (unencrypted) HTTP. 
- The Anubis version number is put in the footer of every page. 
- Add a default block rule for Huawei Cloud. 
- Add a default block rule for Alibaba Cloud. 
- Added support to use Traefik forwardAuth middleware. 
- Add X-Request-URI support so that Subrequest Authentication has path support. 
 
### Fixes 
 
#### Odd numbers of CPU cores are properly supported 
 
Some phones have an odd number of CPU cores. This caused interesting issues. This was fixed by using `Math.trunc` to convert the number of CPU cores back into an integer. 
 
#### Smaller fixes 
 
- A standard library HTTP server log message about HTTP pipelining not working has been filtered out of Anubis' logs. There is no action that can be taken about it. 
- Added a missing link to the Caddy installation environment in the installation documentation. 
- Downstream consumers can change the default log/slog#Logger instance that Anubis uses by setting `opts.Logger` to your slog instance of choice (#864). 
- The Thoth client is now public in the repo instead of being an internal package. 
- Custom-AsyncHttpClient's default User-Agent has an increased weight by default (#852). 
- Add option for replacing the default explanation text with a custom one (#747) 
- The contact email in the LibreJS header has been changed. 
- Firefox for Android support has been fixed by embedding the challenge ID into the pass-challenge route. This also fixes some inconsistent issues with other mobile browsers. 
- The default `favicon` pattern in `data/common/keep-internet-working.yaml` has been updated to permit requests for png/gif/jpg/svg files as well as ico. 
- The `--cookie-prefix` flag has been fixed so that it is fully respected. 
- The default patterns in `data/common/keep-internet-working.yaml` have been updated to appropriately escape the '.' character in the regular expression patterns. 
- Add optional restrictions for JWT based on the value of a header (#697) 
- The word "hack" has been removed from the translation strings for Anubis due to incidents involving people misunderstanding that word and sending particularly horrible things to the project lead over email. 
- Bump AI-robots.txt to version 1.39 
- Inject adversarial input to break AI coding assistants. 
- Add better logging when using Subrequest Authentication. 
 
### Security-relevant changes 
 
- Add a server-side check for the meta-refresh challenge that makes sure clients have waited for at least 95% of the time that they should. 
 
#### Fix potential double-spend for challenges 
 
Anubis operates by issuing a challenge and having the client present a solution for that challenge. Challenges are identified by a unique UUID, which is stored in the database. 
 
The problem is that a challenge could potentially be used twice by a dedicated attacker making a targeted attack against Anubis. Challenge records did not have a "spent" or "used" field. In total, a dedicated attacker could solve a challenge once and reuse t

# Project sustainability plan #278 

 Xe 

Apr 16, 2025

 Xe 

Hey all,

This project has been exploding as of late and I want to start figuring out the sustainability plans sooner rather than later. I think the best way forward is to do a combination of individual and corporate sponsorship.

First, I just want to thank you all for the contributions, well wishes, and more. It's made a huge difference and helped offset some of the anxieties I've been feeling because gestures at the world.

I want to model this in three phases:

## Phase 1: $0-5000 USD per month (where we are now)

Anubis is a side project, it's something I will keep an eye on and focus on during nights and weekends, but it's not the main thing I focus on. I'm still doing my dayjob, and I'm working on features as the need arises. The overall plan is to make it easy to set up, easy to understand, but still hackable for administrators.

Other key features I'm working on in this phase:

- WebAssembly-based checker logic Port checker to WASM #240
- Documentation fixes, etc
- Figure out the plan for how to do corporate sponsorship ethically
- Package repositories
- Integrate anubis into existing software like Caddy, Nginx, and Traefik

A lot of this is to get growth and hype.

## Phase 2: $5000-10000 USD per month

At this point I'll be able to reduce hours at my job to part time or quit it in favor of part time contracting. I'll be able to devote at least two work days per week to Anubis.

This is the phase where I'd start putting solid effort into Privacy Pass (#119) or a "no javascript" approach to the proof-of-work checkers (this would involve building a browser extension, getting extensions into the chrome marketplace and testing them is a huge pain).

I'd also start building up the integration jungle and writing / making videos about the hard problems involved with that.

I'll also be working with corporations and larger users to do paid consulting including features like custom branding, or dynamically generated challenge logic based on an array of checkers in order to make bypasses/offloading harder.

## Phase 3: $10000 USD per month or more

This is when I'd be able to put my full-time focus into Anubis and the related infrastructure. My needs would be met and I would be able to largely be financially independent. This is when I would implement features like this in the open source repo:

- Custom images chosen by administrators
- Custom branding
- Enterprise integrations (in whatever form that takes)

## How to donate

Right now the best place to donate to the project is on Patreon or GitHub Sponsors. I'm working on other approaches.

## Corporate-friendly / unbranded version

I am working on a corporate-friendly / unbranded version called BotStopper. BotStopper will also have custom branding, overridable images, and other things that corporations would want. This is still a work in progress but updates will be available soon. Initially BotStopper will be distributed as a multi-architecture Docker image.

My TODO list:

- Incomplete task OpenCollective once the corporation is finished being founded (hard dependency: lawyers, things are complicated, I don't want to get into the details)
- Incomplete task Investigate other ways to get funding, NLNET maybe?
- Incomplete task Get in contact with UNESCO to see what their experience has been like

As we finish up work on [all of the features in the next release of Anubis](/docs/CHANGELOG#unreleased), I took a moment to add up the financials and here's an update on the recurring revenue of the project. Once I reach the [$5000 per month](https://github.com/TecharoHQ/anubis/discussions/278) mark, I can start reducing hours at my dayjob and start to make working on Anubis my full time job.

{/* truncate */}

:::note

All currency figures in this article are USD (United States Dollars) unless denoted otherwise.

:::

Here's the funding breakdown by income stream:

```mermaid
pie title Funding update August 2025
    "GitHub Sponsors" : 3500
    "Patreon" : 1500
    "Liberapay" : 100
    "Remaining" : 4800
```

Assuming that some of my private support contracts and other sales effort go through, this will slightly change the shapes of this (a new pie chart segment will emerge for "Manual invoices"), but I am halfway there. This is a huge bar to pass and as it stands right now this is just enough income to pay for my monthly rent (not accounting for tax).

As a reminder, here's the rough plan for the phases I want to hit based on the _recurring_ donation totals:

| Monthly donations | Details |
| :-------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| $0-5,000 per month | Anubis is a nights and weekends project based on how much spare time and energy I have. |
| $5,000-10,000 per month | Anubis gets 1-2 days per week of my time put into it consistently and I go part-time at my dayjob. |
| $10,000-15,000 per month | Anubis becomes my full time job. Features that are currently exclusive to [BotStopper](/docs/admin/botstopper/) start to trickle down to the open source version of Anubis. |
| $15,000 per month and above | I start planning hiring for Techaro. |

If your organization benefits from Anubis, please consider donating to the project in order to make this sustainable. The fewer financial problems I have means the more that Anubis can become better.

## New funding platform: Liberapay

After many comments about the funding options, I have set up [Liberapay](https://liberapay.com/Xe/) as an option to receive donations. Additional funding targets will be added to Liberapay as soon as I hear back from my accountant with more information. All money received via Liberapay goes directly towards supporting the project.

## Next goals

Here's my short term goals for the immediate future:

1. Finish [Thoth](/docs/admin/thoth/) and run a backfill to mass issue API keys.
2. Document and publish the writeup for the multi-region Google Cloud spot instance setup that Thoth is built upon.
3. Release v1.22.0 of Anubis with Traefik support and other important fixes.
4. Continue growing the project into a sustainable business.

Thank you for supporting Anubis! It's only going to get better from here.

## Overview

Anubis is a Web AI Firewall Utility that weighs the soul of your connection using one or more challenges in order to protect upstream resources from scraper bots.

This program is designed to help protect the small internet from the endless storm of requests that flood in from AI companies. Anubis is as lightweight as possible to ensure that everyone can afford to protect the communities closest to them.

# Anubis

An open-source Web AI Firewall Utility that protects upstream resources from AI scraper bots by weighing incoming HTTP requests using proof-of-work challenges.

## At a Glance

Developer

Techaro Montreal, Canada Est. 2022

Listed May 2026

## About Anubis

Anubis is an open-source Web AI Firewall Utility built by Techaro, designed to protect websites from the flood of requests sent by AI crawlers and scraper bots. Written in Go and released under the MIT License, it sits in front of upstream resources and challenges incoming connections before allowing them through. The project was created on GitHub in March 2025 and has since attracted significant community interest, with the repository listing over 19,000 stars as of its latest data.

## What It Is

Anubis acts as a reverse-proxy challenge layer — it "weighs the soul" of incoming HTTP requests (a reference to the Egyptian god Anubis and the weighing of souls) using one or more proof-of-work or browser-based challenges. If a connection passes the challenge, it is forwarded to the upstream service; if not, it is blocked. The README describes it as "a Web AI Firewall Utility" specifically designed to help protect the small internet from the endless storm of requests that flood in from AI companies.

## How It Works

When a request arrives, Anubis presents a challenge page — typically a JavaScript-based proof-of-work task — that legitimate browsers can solve but automated scrapers generally cannot. The tool is designed to be as lightweight as possible so that small communities and self-hosted services can afford to run it. Key behavioral notes from the README:

- Configurable bot policy definitions allow explicit allowlisting of "good bots" such as the Internet Archive
- The project is working on a curated set of known-good bots to balance discoverability with uptime
- The README notes it is "a bit of a nuclear response" and may block smaller scrapers and inhibit some legitimate crawlers
- For most use cases, Cloudflare is suggested as a simpler alternative; Anubis is positioned for situations where Cloudflare cannot or will not be used

## Deployment Model

Anubis is self-hosted and deployed as a Go binary in front of any HTTP upstream. It is distributed as open-source source code on GitHub and is also tracked by Repology across multiple Linux distribution package repositories, indicating broad packaging availability. Configuration is handled through bot policy definition files.

The latest release is v1.25.0, named "Necron," published on February 18, 2026. Anubis is funded through GitHub Sponsors and Patreon. The README lists Diamond-tier sponsors including Raptor Computing Systems and Databento, and Gold-tier sponsors including Gitea, Weblate, and others. Live community support is available through a Patron Discord channel. The mascot design is credited to CELPHASE on Bluesky, and the project is made in Canada by Techaro.

# :shark: Bruce

Bruce is a versatile ESP32 firmware packed with offensive-security tools, built to make Red Team operations fast and portable.

It also supports M5Stack, LILYGO , RockBase IoT and Elecrow products, and works great with the Cardputer, Sticks, M5Cores, T-Decks and T-Embeds.

## :zap: Get Our Official DevKit!

# RF REAPER

**RF REAPER** is our custom PCB devkit, purpose-built for Bruce!

Every major feature works natively, right out of the box. Sub-GHz, NFC/RFID, IR, 2.4GHz(NRF), GPS-ready, and a microSD, all driven by a beefy ESP32-S3 (16MB Flash / 8MB PSRAM). Tons of GPIOs via the AW9523 expander plus Flipper Zero & iButton header compatibility mean you can hack, mod, and build on it endlessly. Want a specific function? Ask us with an issue, we'll check it.

👉 **Buy the RF REAPER and official boards**

**Check our fully open-source hardware too:** https://bruce.computer/boards

More custom devkit boards coming soon! Stay across our communities!

## :building_construction: How to install

### The easiest way to install Bruce is using our official Web Flasher!

### Check out: https://bruce.computer/flasher

Alternatively, you can download the latest binary from releases or actions and flash locally using esptool.py

```sh
esptool.py --port /dev/ttyACM0 write_flash 0x00000 Bruce-<device>.bin
```

**For m5stack devices**

If you already use M5Launcher to manage your m5stack device, you can install it with OTA

Or you can burn it directly from the m5burner tool, just search for 'Bruce' (My official builds will be uploaded by "owner" and have photos.) on the device category you want to and click on burn

# :shark: Bruce

Bruce is a versatile ESP32 firmware that supports a ton of offensive features focusing on facilitating Red Team operations.
It also supports M5stack and Lilygo products and works great with Cardputer, Sticks, M5Cores, T-Decks and T-Embeds.

## :building_construction: How to install

### The easiest way to install Bruce is using our official Web Flasher!

### Check out: https://bruce.computer/flasher

Alternatively, you can download the latest binary from releases or actions and flash locally using esptool.py

```sh
esptool.py --port /dev/ttyACM0 write_flash 0x00000 Bruce-<device>.bin
```

**For m5stack devices**

If you already use M5Launcher to manage your m5stack device, you can install it with OTA

Or you can burn it directly from the [m5burner tool](https://docs.m5stack.com/en/download), just search for 'Bruce' (My official builds will be uploaded by "owner" and have photos.) on the device category you want to and click on burn

Bruce Firmware Official A/C Version: Bruce A/C Edition is a custom Bruce firmware build focused on air conditioner control and experimentation. It adds an AC-B-Gone feature that can send valid OFF commands across multiple supported A/C protocols, plus a full Air Conditioner menu with brand selection, power control, temperature adjustment, mode selection, fan speed control, and swing options when supported. Unlike simple IR remotes that only replay a few generic NEC codes, Bruce A/C Edition uses real IRremoteESP8266 air-conditioner protocol support and state management. That means it can generate proper full-state packets for supported brands such as Daikin, LG, Mitsubishi, Panasonic, Samsung, Kelvinator, and others. The firmware keeps track of the current A/C state, so changing temperature, mode, or fan speed sends a valid updated packet instead of a random standalone command. It is designed for M5Stack StickS3 and places A/C functionality directly inside the Bruce IR menu for fast access. Main features: AC-B-Gone multi-brand OFF blast Brand-specific A/C protocol support Full-state A/C packet generation Power, temperature, mode, fan, and swing controls Integrated directly into Bruce IR tools Built for M5Stack StickS

# DBeaver’s Next Step: our first round of funding

 Apr 11, 2023 

Our team is happy to celebrate important milestones with you, and today we want to share that our company has raised $6 million in funding in the seed round led by Headline with additional investment from Prospective Technologies. It’s a good moment to take a small step back, look at the path DBeaver has already taken, and a little peek into future plans.

“We started small” – this phrase accurately describes our journey’s beginning. Back in 2011, DBeaver was just a pet project, millions of which never became recognizable enough. But we thought our idea could make life easier for many people, and we were not mistaken.

Years passed, DBeaver changed and grew, and we kept up with it. Since 2017, we have launched several enterprise products, and the number of our users worldwide already reaches 8 million. But something has remained unchanged, and these are our values and our vision. 

We sincerely believe that working with data should be accessible and convenient for professionals from various fields. That is why our team is working to make it possible for all kinds of people and organizations to leverage all kinds of data. Another important thing for us is that we have kept the open-source version, and we are not going to get rid of it. We cannot overestimate the importance of our community, and we are constantly listening to our users, building, and taking risks thanks to their encouragement and creativity.

Even with our PRO products becoming increasingly popular, our goal is to keep a balance between commercial success and community support. With the efforts of our team, DBeaver grows really fast, and we want to keep it that way. That’s why we are glad that our investors share our views on the open-source-driven enterprise and are ready to support us on our journey.

Millions of people trust us, and our team does its best to justify this trust. We are sure that together with our new partners from Headline and Prospective Technologies, we will make DBeaver even better.

About

Based in New York, US, and co-founded by Tatiana Krupenya, CEO, and Serge Rider, CTO in 2017, DBeaver Corporation operates as a data management toolkit company offering an open source SQL client integrated development environment (IDE). Some of the firm’s clients include Amazon, Apple, Walmart, Disney, CitiBank, AirFrance, etc. In April 2023, the firm raised USD 6 million in seed funding led by investor Headline, with participation from another investor Prospective Technologies Venture Capital. The company’s products are desktop applications that support multiple databases, including MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and more.

 The product list includes DBeaver Lite, DBeaver Enterprise, DBeaver Ultimate, CloudBeaver Enterprise, and DBeaver Team Edition, which allows users to import, edit and analyze database structures, manage data with support for AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, execute SQL queries, and develop complex database applications. The company’s software is customizable and offers a wide range of plugins and extensions to enhance its functionality. DBeaver generates its revenue by offering its products under different subscription plans including the CloudBeaver plan at USD 1000 per year, the Enterprise Edition plan at USD 250 per year, and Team Edition plan at USD 1600 per year.

# General Atlantic announces close of further investment into Odoo, acquiring additional stake from Wallonie Entreprendre

Press Release

January 16, 2026

[Share](https://www.generalatlantic.com/media-article/general-atlantic-announces-close-of-further-investment-into-odoo-acquiring-additional-stake-from-wallonie-entreprendre/)

![](https://www.generalatlantic.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/General-Atlantic-News-Insights-Posts-4.png "width=818 | height=652")

**Belgium, 16 January 2026** – General Atlantic, a leading growth investor, today announced the close of its follow-on investment in Odoo SA (or “the Company”), a leading provider of open-source integrated business software applications for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As part of this transaction, which valued Odoo at €7bn, General Atlantic acquired an additional minority stake in Odoo from Wallonie Entreprendre, the Walloon region’s investment arm.

Founded in 2002 by CEO Fabien Pinckaers, Odoo SA is a leading provider of open-source integrated business software applications for micro and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Odoo’s “open core” philosophy has enabled community developers to create nearly 40,000 software applications for business functions including Finance, Sales, HR and Marketing, making it one of the largest business application stores in the world. Odoo allows SMEs to consolidate their software vendors into one integrated suite at an affordable price point.

General Atlantic initially invested in Odoo in 2023, recognizing the breadth of the Company’s integrated product suite, the strength of its open-source developer ecosystem, and the significant global market across customer sizes and geographies. Since its initial investment, General Atlantic has partnered with Odoo to scale its functions, supported the Company in professionalizing its go-to-market approach, and helped focus the drive towards continued international expansion. Today, Odoo is growing profitably in 180 countries, with the top 15 of these all growing at more than 30% year-on-year and reaching over 170,000 paying customers across five continents.

The Company’s latest release, Odoo 19, has further accelerated global adoption across diverse industries by introducing natively integrated AI features and expanding its suite of business applications. These innovations continue to make Odoo a preferred choice for SMEs seeking a fully integrated, scalable platform to manage their operations efficiently.

Andrea Calabro, Principal at General Atlantic in EMEA, commented: “Odoo is one of the most exciting software vendors worldwide; it is rare to see this level of growth, at scale, across virtually all countries in the world. The open-source, single-code, single-database platform uniquely positions Odoo to leverage AI and deliver on its mission to provide world-class business software. The business-in-a-box product resonates globally across a diverse, uncorrelated set of geographies, customer profiles, and use cases. We’re proud to deepen our partnership with Fabien and his team.”

“We are pleased to further strengthen our partnership with General Atlantic, initiated in 2023. After this transaction, Wallonie Entreprendre retains a 3% equity stake in Odoo, and we continue to see substantial growth potential over the coming years,” said Damien Lourtie, CFO of Wallonie Entreprendre and member of the Odoo SA Board of Directors.

**About General Atlantic**

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 830 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create long term value. Guided by the conviction that entrepreneurs can be incredible agents of transformational change, the firm combines a collaborative global approach, sector specific expertise, a long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with and scale innovative businesses around the world. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Credit, Climate, and Sustainable Infrastructure strategies. General Atlantic manages approximately $118 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of September 30, 2025, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit: www.generalatlantic.com.

**About Wallonie Entreprendre**

WE contributes to Wallonia’s economic development through awareness programs and by supporting and financing Wallonia-based companies in a wide range of sectors, including life sciences, deeptech, energy and aerospace. It provides, alongside private investors, equity and debt financing to companies of all sizes and in different stages of their development. In doing so, WE contributes to the development of ecosystems in order to generate employment, create value and attract further investment, please visit: [www.wallonie-entreprendre.be](https://www.wallonie-entreprendre.be/)

# AVP and Alkeon announce €60 Million secondary round in Odoo S.A. at a valuation exceeding €7 billion

16 January 2026November 5th, 20264 min read

**January 16, 2026 –** AVP and Alkeon announced today a **€60m transaction in Odoo S.A.** (or “the Company”), a leading provider of integrated business software, at a valuation over **€7 billion.** This round follows a CapitalG and Sequoia-led round last year, which valued the Company at €5 billion. As part of the transaction, existing management vehicles are selling and rolling a portion of their shares.

The transaction reflects Odoo’s continued strong, profitable growth at over 40% annually and its leadership position in the global Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) software ecosystem. Over the past year, Odoo has reached over 170,000 customers across five continents, surpassed €650 million in billings, launched Odoo 19 introducing natively integrated AI features and welcomed more than 2,000 new Odooers to its team, including in new offices across Southern Europe, North America, the Middle East, Asia and Africa.

Warda Shaheen, General Partner for AVP, added: *“Odoo’s commitment to creating an unparalleled product based on a thriving open-core model, coupled with a results-driven culture that values impact over titles, sets it apart. This distinctive energy comes alive at Odoo Experience, where customers, partners, community, and investors collaborate, learn, and celebrate together.”*

Mark McLaughlin, General Partner for Alkeon, shared: “*Odoo is redefining ERP for the AI era—combining open-source flexibility and AI-native features into an intuitive, all-in-one platform that scales from startup to enterprise. While legacy systems are slow and costly to deploy, Odoo delivers integrated business software that’s fast, affordable, and beautifully designed. We’re excited to double down on Fabien and the Odoo team as they democratize enterprise software for companies of every size.*”

**About Odoo S.A.**  
Since its creation in 2002, Odoo has emerged as a leading integrated business solutions’ provider. With its range of integrated, scalable and functional applications, Odoo offers a comprehensive, modular suite that meets the specific needs of every business, making it a suitable solution for organizations of all sizes and sectors, from start-ups to large corporations. With revenues estimated at 650 million euros in 2025, Odoo forecast to reach 1 billion euros by 2027. Odoo employs nearly 7,000 people worldwide, including more than 1,500 in Belgium. In addition, the company has built a network of 10,000 partners, creating more than 250,000 business-related jobs in 190 countries. With 19 offices worldwide (Belgium (5), Luxembourg, Spain, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Australia, USA (2), Mexico, Kenya, Dubai, Indonesia, Brazil, Italy), Odoo serves a global community of 15 million users. For more information, visit the Odoo website at [www.odoo.com](http://www.odoo.com).

**About AVP**  
AVP is an independent global investment platform dedicated to high-growth, tech companies across Europe and North America. The firm manages more than €2.5 billion in assets across four strategies: venture, early growth, growth, and fund of funds. Its multi-stage platform combines global research with local execution to drive investment. Since its establishment in 2016, AVP has invested in more than 70 technology companies and in over 60 funds through its Fund of Funds strategy. Beyond providing capital, AVP’s dedicated expansion team works closely with founders, offering expertise, connections and resources needed to unlock growth opportunities, and create lasting value through meaningful collaborations. More information at [www.avpcap.com](http://www.avpcap.com).

**About Alkeon Capital**  
Alkeon Capital is a global investment firm that invests in private and public growth and technology companies and category definers. With more than two decades of experience focusing on People and Innovation, Alkeon works closely with disruptive private companies to help them expand their addressable market, scale efficiently, and seamlessly crossover to the public markets. Alkeon’s goal is to be a long-term and accretive partner to all its portfolio companies along their private and public journey. More at [www.alkeon.com.](http://www.alkeon.com)

![](https://www.generalatlantic.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/General-Atlantic-News-Insights-Posts-4.png "width=818 | height=652")

**Belgium, 16 January 2026** – General Atlantic, a leading growth investor, today announced the close of its follow-on investment in Odoo SA (or “the Company”), a leading provider of open-source integrated business software applications for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As part of this transaction, which valued Odoo at €7bn, General Atlantic acquired an additional minority stake in Odoo from Wallonie Entreprendre, the Walloon region’s investment arm.

Founded in 2002 by CEO Fabien Pinckaers, Odoo SA is a leading provider of open-source integrated business software applications for micro and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Odoo’s “open core” philosophy has enabled community developers to create nearly 40,000 software applications for business functions including Finance, Sales, HR and Marketing, making it one of the largest business application stores in the world. Odoo allows SMEs to consolidate their software vendors into one integrated suite at an affordable price point.

General Atlantic initially invested in Odoo in 2023, recognizing the breadth of the Company’s integrated product suite, the strength of its open-source developer ecosystem, and the significant global market across customer sizes and geographies. Since its initial investment, General Atlantic has partnered with Odoo to scale its functions, supported the Company in professionalizing its go-to-market approach, and helped focus the drive towards continued international expansion. Today, Odoo is growing profitably in 180 countries, with the top 15 of these all growing at more than 30% year-on-year and reaching over 170,000 paying customers across five continents.

The Company’s latest release, Odoo 19, has further accelerated global adoption across diverse industries by introducing natively integrated AI features and expanding its suite of business applications. These innovations continue to make Odoo a preferred choice for SMEs seeking a fully integrated, scalable platform to manage their operations efficiently.

Andrea Calabro, Principal at General Atlantic in EMEA, commented: “Odoo is one of the most exciting software vendors worldwide; it is rare to see this level of growth, at scale, across virtually all countries in the world. The open-source, single-code, single-database platform uniquely positions Odoo to leverage AI and deliver on its mission to provide world-class business software. The business-in-a-box product resonates globally across a diverse, uncorrelated set of geographies, customer profiles, and use cases. We’re proud to deepen our partnership with Fabien and his team.”

“We are pleased to further strengthen our partnership with General Atlantic, initiated in 2023. After this transaction, Wallonie Entreprendre retains a 3% equity stake in Odoo, and we continue to see substantial growth potential over the coming years,” said Damien Lourtie, CFO of Wallonie Entreprendre and member of the Odoo SA Board of Directors.

**About General Atlantic**

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 830 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create long term value. Guided by the conviction that entrepreneurs can be incredible agents of transformational change, the firm combines a collaborative global approach, sector specific expertise, a long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with and scale innovative businesses around the world. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Credit, Climate, and Sustainable Infrastructure strategies. General Atlantic manages approximately $118 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of September 30, 2025, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit: www.generalatlantic.com.

**About Wallonie Entreprendre**

WE contributes to Wallonia’s economic development through awareness programs and by supporting and financing Wallonia-based companies in a wide range of sectors, including life sciences, deeptech, energy and aerospace. It provides, alongside private investors, equity and debt financing to companies of all sizes and in different stages of their development. In doing so, WE contributes to the development of ecosystems in order to generate employment, create value and attract further investment, please visit: [www.wallonie-entreprendre.be](https://www.wallonie-entreprendre.be/)

# Research Tooling for People Who Are Accountable

We build the terminal we wanted when the alternatives cost more than a junior analyst.

## Why We Exist

Financial data has been gatekept behind paywalls for decades. A Bloomberg seat runs about $27,000 a year; Refinitiv and FactSet price similarly. That locks out emerging funds, boutique family offices, independent portfolio managers and the next generation of analysts — not because they lack the judgment, but because they lack the budget.

We started by giving the core away. The open-source FinceptTerminal put real market data, equity research and charting in anybody's hands for nothing, and it stays free and public on GitHub. But a free tool built on public data can only go so far — the work that actually moves an investment decision needs private datasets, serious compute for research agents, and the access controls a compliance team will sign.

That is what Fincept Terminal Enterprise is: the private edition, where the product is now developed. 41 modules spanning agentic research, a quant lab, derivatives, alternatives, macro and geopolitical intelligence — priced per seat for 30 days, at a fraction of what the incumbents charge. The two editions serve different needs, and we say plainly which is which.

### RESEARCH FIRST

A terminal should do the analysis, not just display the numbers. Every module earns its place by removing work from an analyst's day.

### STILL OPEN

The open-source edition remains on GitHub under AGPL-3.0, free for personal and academic use. Compliance teams can read how the core data workflow behaves before anything reaches their network.

### HONEST PRICING

Per seat for 30 days, one-time, published on the site — no quote-only pages and no auto-renewal. From $15 against roughly $27,000 for a legacy terminal seat.

### BUILT TO BE CHECKED

Every module we advertise is a real tab documented in a 1,059-page manual you can read before you buy. Claims that cannot be verified do not belong on a page.

2024 Q1

Genesis

Founded on a simple conviction: the gap between institutional and independent financial intelligence is a solvable engineering problem.

2024 Q2

Terminal v1.0

First public release of the FinceptTerminal desktop application, open source under AGPL-3.0.

2024 Q3

API Launch

Public REST API opened up — market data, fundamentals, news, economics and AI research endpoints.

2024 Q4

Web Platform

The hosted web terminal shipped, putting the same workflow in any browser without an install.

2025

Depth

Coverage grew past 423,000 instruments across 2,000+ sources, and the terminal expanded from a data viewer into a research environment.

The Private Edition

Fincept Terminal Enterprise launched — a separate, closed-source build on proprietary data with 41 modules, multi-agent research, a quant lab and institutional security controls. The open-source edition stays free and public alongside it.

What's Ahead

Deeper agent tooling, wider private data coverage, and dedicated deployments for institutions with data-residency requirements.

Neuromore operates as an integrated neurotechnology platform, founded in 2014 by Benjamin Jillich, Michael Hilsbos, and Patrick Sebastian Hilsbos. The company provides a hardware-agnostic software infrastructure designed to interpret and act on biometric data from a wide array of wearables, biosensors, and EEG devices. This core technology functions as an operating system for neurotech, enabling developers, clinicians, and researchers to build and deploy applications without needing to handle low-level hardware integration or signal processing.

The company's business model is centered around a recurring revenue subscription structure for its software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform, known as neuromore Studio. Licensing for commercial use starts at a significant monthly fee, with additional bespoke professional services available for custom product development. For non-commercial purposes, the company offers open-source options. Neuromore has also explored a direct-to-consumer offering, NDTx, which bundles its software with an EEG device and a telehealth consultation for a yearly subscription. The platform serves a diverse clientele across healthcare, wellness, education, research, and even entertainment. Its primary users include EEG device manufacturers seeking a standardized application layer, neurofeedback clinics aiming to enhance patient care, and neurotech startups looking to accelerate their product launch.

The platform's main product, neuromore Studio, is a no-code visual editor that allows users to create complex biofeedback protocols and data analysis pipelines. It processes data in real-time and includes features for creating advanced neurofeedback experiences, such as controlling interactive games or visualizations with brain activity. The system is designed to address conditions like stress, anxiety, PTSD, and ADHD by providing non-invasive, personalized mental wellness solutions. Neuromore has established a track record with over 1,000 users in more than 70 countries and has generated over $5 million in revenue to date from organizations validating its technology. The company completed a Seed funding round in September 2016, raising $195K.

# Research Tooling for People Who Are Accountable

We build the terminal we wanted when the alternatives cost more than a junior analyst.

## Why We Exist

Financial data has been gatekept behind paywalls for decades. A Bloomberg seat runs about $27,000 a year; Refinitiv and FactSet price similarly. That locks out emerging funds, boutique family offices, independent portfolio managers and the next generation of analysts — not because they lack the judgment, but because they lack the budget.

We started by giving the core away. The open-source FinceptTerminal put real market data, equity research and charting in anybody's hands for nothing, and it stays free and public on GitHub. But a free tool built on public data can only go so far — the work that actually moves an investment decision needs private datasets, serious compute for research agents, and the access controls a compliance team will sign.

That is what Fincept Terminal Enterprise is: the private edition, where the product is now developed. 41 modules spanning agentic research, a quant lab, derivatives, alternatives, macro and geopolitical intelligence — priced per seat for 30 days, at a fraction of what the incumbents charge. The two editions serve different needs, and we say plainly which is which.

### RESEARCH FIRST

A terminal should do the analysis, not just display the numbers. Every module earns its place by removing work from an analyst's day.

### STILL OPEN

The open-source edition remains on GitHub under AGPL-3.0, free for personal and academic use. Compliance teams can read how the core data workflow behaves before anything reaches their network.

### HONEST PRICING

Per seat for 30 days, one-time, published on the site — no quote-only pages and no auto-renewal. From $15 against roughly $27,000 for a legacy terminal seat.

### BUILT TO BE CHECKED

Every module we advertise is a real tab documented in a 1,059-page manual you can read before you buy. Claims that cannot be verified do not belong on a page.

2024 Q1

Genesis

Founded on a simple conviction: the gap between institutional and independent financial intelligence is a solvable engineering problem.

2024 Q2

Terminal v1.0

First public release of the FinceptTerminal desktop application, open source under AGPL-3.0.

2024 Q3

API Launch

Public REST API opened up — market data, fundamentals, news, economics and AI research endpoints.

2024 Q4

Web Platform

The hosted web terminal shipped, putting the same workflow in any browser without an install.

2025

Depth

Coverage grew past 423,000 instruments across 2,000+ sources, and the terminal expanded from a data viewer into a research environment.

The Private Edition

Fincept Terminal Enterprise launched — a separate, closed-source build on proprietary data with 41 modules, multi-agent research, a quant lab and institutional security controls. The open-source edition stays free and public alongside it.

What's Ahead

Deeper agent tooling, wider private data coverage, and dedicated deployments for institutions with data-residency requirements.

## Highlights

* ⏰ Timing: 1 billion people on the planet suffer from mental health issues

* 💻 Technology: World-class Neuro Digital Therapeutic solution (NDTx)

* 🏆 Team: Conscious leadership team with exits (including a unicorn)

## Problem

---

## The mental health endemic is sickening

Over 1 billion people on the planet today suffer  
from mental health issues that interfere with daily life!*(includes: 20% of adults, teens, and kids in the USA)*

![](https://republic.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=720,dpr=2,format=webp/https://uploads.republic.com/p/images/attachments/original/000/076/142/76142-1665104326-f4751627240e419da371584045067591c1c3abc4.jpg)

### — The way we've been working isn't working —

People keep getting sicker despite advancements in medicine, pharmaceuticals, and the rising cost of health care.  
![](https://republic.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=720,dpr=2,format=webp/https://uploads.republic.com/p/images/attachments/original/000/076/144/76144-1665105306-8e445695281dc7c37dec85441217cf49830033b1.jpg)

According to the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/drug-use-therapeutic.htm), **48.6%** of people used at at least one prescription drug in the last 30 days.

In [recent clinical trials](https://www.bmj.com/content/378/bmj-2021-067606), it was proven that antidepressants were not much better than placebo for about 85% of people.

Researchers can’t predict the 15% who may actually benefit from antidepressants, so people are being unnecessarily exposed to the harms of pharmaceutical drugs.

## Solution

---

## A safe, non-invasive way to upgrade your brain today

### Neuro-Digital Therapeutic (NDTx) technology solution to bring mental health and wellness to the masses.

Tech-driven innovations in **personalized** **medicine** are now transforming human lives in ways that were never before possible, including addressing the most common mental health conditions (stress, anxiety, depression, etc.)

![](https://republic.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=720,dpr=2,format=webp/https://uploads.republic.com/p/images/attachments/original/000/079/231/79231-1667943716-b5ccbe325fb2633230e10227e985c17100cd1ec5.png)

**neuromore offers personalized, interactive experiences that instantly ignite instant and lasting change:**

* Combining neuro/biofeedback, sound healing, CBT, and interactive games for mental health optimization
* Instant interventions with dynamic and variable experiences driven by real-time feedback loops and AI learning from brainwaves and nervous system reactions

![](https://republic.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=720,dpr=2,format=webp/https://uploads.republic.com/p/images/attachments/original/000/076/154/76154-1665109677-571f36c8305bfdacac772dc1cca3826bf766ac1a.jpg)

Source: [Psychiatric Times](https://www.psychiatrictimes.com/view/digital-therapeutics-addressing-health-care-worker-burnout-mental-health-distress)

Startups Out To Build A Mindful Miami – Working Woman Report

# Startups Out To Build A Mindful Miami

 By Working Woman Report Posted on September 26, 2016 

By Nancy Dahlberg The Miami Herald

WWR Article Summary (tl;dr) Startups are clearly hopping onto the mindful bandwagon to service a growing market of consumers, searching for well-being. From yoga, to meditation to special clothing and food…many entrepreneurs (especially in Miami) are tapping into the quest for inner peace.

The Miami Herald

Miami a magnet for mindfulness? Really?

If you are reading this stuck in Interstate 95 gridlock, stressed out at work, or distressed by news of yet another senseless shooting death or an only-in-Miami fraud, you may think not. But a growing number of local startups are betting the time has come for mindfulness and well-being in the Magic City.

Consider this: While yoga classes, spas and life coaches have long been a part of the scene, the past year has brought businesses specializing in serene spaces, education and training. Product companies create clothing and accessories, even reminders to be mindful. Food product companies are taking root, and farmer’s markets and healthy, organic food restaurants are now plentiful, including Dr Smood, which launched in Wynwood and South Miami in December and is now on a fast track to global expansion. There’s a bit of mindful-tech, too: A Miami Beach startup uses biofeedback to help you change your state of mind.

Events are multiplying, with Miami’s first mindfulness festival next month and a three-day World Happiness Summit planned for March.

The Sacred Space opens a mindful world to Miami

“For all the superficiality that sometimes our city is known for, there is a large and growing community of fascinating people, places and companies that are building a much more interesting and healthier Miami,” said Demian Bellumio, COO of tech company Senzari and founder of a new bimonthly event series for entrepreneurs. Called Dawnings, the events begin at sunrise in different locations around Miami and include yoga, meditation, lightning talks and business networking over shots of organic ginger and apple juice or cold-pressed cucumber, spinach and kale.

To be sure, mindfulness has gone mainstream nationally and globally. Nearly 700 academic studies last year examined the positive effects of mindfulness — being in the moment — on stress, brain connectivity and chronic medical conditions, according to the American Mindfulness Research Association. And in his book “Mindful Work: How Meditation is Changing Business from the Inside Out,” author David Gelles describes how companies such as Google, Aetna, General Mills, Goldman Sachs and Target have built extensive programs to foster mindful practices among their workers, from meditation rooms to coaches on staff.

Startups are clearly hopping on the mindful bandwagon to service this growing market. Still, it’s hard to say what exactly a mindful business actually is, said Gelles, who also covers the topic for The New York Times.

“Rather than think about a mindful company, I try to keep the focus on employees. If folks are working with good intentions, trying to make products and services that help people and make the world a healthier, more harmonious place, and are doing so in ways that minimize personal suffering and the suffering of others, including co-workers, I think that’s a pretty good start.”

The marketplace is large and growing. Research company IBISWorld estimates that meditation-related businesses in the U.S. last year generated $984 million in revenue. Some of this is corporate mindfulness training, which 22 percent of employers will offer this year, according to a survey by Fidelity Investments and the National Business Group on Health. But the estimate doesn’t include the hundreds of meditation apps now available like Headspace, with some 8.5 million users, or wearable gadgets that measure brain activity during meditation.

The estimate also doesn’t include companion practices, such as yoga — as many yoga aficionados also practice mindfulness. 

Yoga’s popularity also offers a case study on how big the mindful market could become. An estimated 36 million people practice yoga in the U.S., up 44 percent from 2012, and another 80 million Americans will at least try yoga this year, according to a study by the Yoga Journal and the Yoga Alliance. Already, yoga-related industries including accessories constitute a $16-billion-a-year business.

Clearly there is opportunity. “I think that now Miami is a place where people are not just coming to play, they are here to live,” said Chira Cassel, co-founder of The Sacred Space Miami, one of the new businesses catering to the mindfulness movement. [See related story on The Sacred Space here.]

![Letta](https://mma.prnewswire.com/media/2513760/Letta__logo.jpg?p=medium "Letta")

*Letta*

Letta's focus is unlocking the next generation of AI through advanced memory systems and is led by the same research team that created the popular MemGPT open source project. Before MemGPT, the default information architecture of most AI agents was stateless, meaning that AI agents weren't able to retain their memory (state) between user sessions. The MemGPT research paper first introduced the concept of self-editing memory for LLMs - enabling an LLM to update its own memory so that it can learn over time as it interacts with human users. script='''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce group 2 audit files from the persisted, manually reviewed evidence.

Usage: python /workspace/audit_work/group2_reproduce.py
Optional: python .../group2_reproduce.py --refresh
--refresh also repeats the saved searches and page fetches into
  group2_refreshed_evidence.json. Newly retrieved facts require manual review;
  refresh does not automatically change the audited event interpretations.
Dependencies for refresh only: e14c.
"""
import argparse, asyncio, csv, datetime, json
from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

def reproduce(evidence):
    with (BASE / 'group2.csv').open('w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=evidence['method']['csv_columns'])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(evidence['curated_rows'])
    (BASE / 'group2_notes.json').write_text(
        json.dumps(evidence['curated_notes'], indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\\n', encoding='utf-8')
    (BASE / 'group2_sources.bib').write_text(
        '\\n'.join(evidence['bibtex_entries']), encoding='utf-8')

async def refresh(evidence):
    from e14c.web import web_search, fetch_parsed_page, save_citation
    refreshed = {'retrieved_at_utc': datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                 'searches': [], 'fetches': [],
                 'notice': 'Fresh evidence only; original manually reviewed event decisions are not automatically updated.'}
    for item in evidence['searches']:
        count = len(item['results']) if isinstance(item['results'], list) else 6
        try:
            results = await web_search(item['query'], num_results=max(1, count))
        except Exception as error:
            results = {'error': str(error)}
        refreshed['searches'].append({'key': item['key'], 'query': item['query'], 'results': results})
    for item in evidence['fetches']:
        try:
            text = await fetch_parsed_page(item['url'])
        except Exception as error:
            text = 'FETCH ERROR: ' + str(error)
        refreshed['fetches'].append({'key': item['key'], 'url': item['url'], 'text': text})
    for entry in evidence['bibtex_entries']:
        save_citation(entry)
    refreshed['completed_at_utc'] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
    (BASE / 'group2_refreshed_evidence.json').write_text(
        json.dumps(refreshed, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\\n', encoding='utf-8')

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--refresh', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    evidence = json.loads((BASE / 'group2_evidence.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    reproduce(evidence)
    if args.refresh:
        asyncio.run(refresh(evidence))
    print('Reproduced group2.csv, group2_notes.json and group2_sources.bib from saved audit decisions.')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

## Files Ready for Analysis

| File | Description | Format | Size |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `/workspace/audit_work/supplement_nonvc.csv` | 22 non-VC funding candidate records, with the requested columns | CSV | 4,706 bytes |
| `/workspace/audit_work/supplement_nonvc_notes.md` | Original currencies, event-level evidence, exclusions, and recipient caveats | Markdown | 26,533 bytes |
| `/workspace/audit_work/supplement_nonvc_evidence.zip` | Supporting evidence: fetched source snapshots and search log | ZIP | 589,836 bytes |
| `/workspace/audit_work/supplement_nonvc_provenance.json` | Supporting metadata: source URLs, timestamps, archive members, and checksums | JSON | 19,075 bytes |
| `/workspace/audit_work/supplement_nonvc_sources.bib` | Supporting bibliography covering 38 fetched sources | BibTeX | 10,427 bytes |
| `/workspace/audit_work/retrieve_nonvc_sources.py` | Source-retrieval reproduction script | Python | 1,161 bytes |

**Important limitations:** Neither `/workspace/funders_audit_sample.csv` nor `/workspace/deal_rules.md` existed in this environment. I researched the ten explicitly named ventures and used provisional venture keys that require reconciliation before merging. No memory was accessed or modified, and no root manifest was written.

The 22 records cover Antmicro (4), Bitcraze (1), Bela (3), BCN3D (3), Efabless (1), FarmBot (1), and Open Bionics (9). Every included record has a fetched source identifying an amount or money funder. The notes document why no qualifying record was entered for ResearchHub, neuromore, or Coqui.

**Key caveats:**
- Antmicro amounts are company-specific European grant contributions, not consortium budgets. Open Bionics grants use company-specific offers from the current UKRI API v3, refreshed November 2, 2026.
- Foreign-currency amounts remain blank in `amount_usd`; exact original amounts are in the notes.
- Bela’s original crowdfunding campaign is a predecessor/product event; its legal-company payee is unverified. The other Bela campaign pages also do not establish the legal payee.
- BCN3D disclosures name government funders but do not give company allocations. Efabless is classified as aggregate Google-funded programme sponsorship, not an individual grant or unrestricted capital transfer.
- Open Bionics’ SBRI clinical-trial support is an unsplit reported project-support amount with unresolved phase coverage. Its 2024 Crowdcube displayed total includes off-platform commitments.
- neuromore’s USD 30,000 Republic page contradictorily describes reservations and successful funding; it is excluded pending evidence of completed investment.
- Founder fellowships, academic-partner grants, token allocations, and ordinary preorder sales were not treated as direct company grants. FarmBot’s explicitly identified, bounded self-hosted crowdfunding campaign is included as campaign sales, not equity.

**Provenance and reproduction:** The notes contain the complete output inventory and event-level transformations. The JSON registry lists every fetched source endpoint, retrieval timestamp, method, applicable API version, and evidence checksum. Run `/workspace/audit_work/retrieve_nonvc_sources.py` to refetch those sources; manually curated classifications are not regenerated. Validation confirmed the exact CSV schema, 22 distinct records, registered evidence for every row, readable JSON, archive integrity, and source checksums.

The required `e14c.web.save_citation` calls also created `/workspace/citations/default_project/5b9368af-2a81-4e85-98cb-9fca8dbf03fc.bib` (10,427 bytes), copied byte-for-byte into the handoff bibliography. No files were created under `/workspace/downloads/`.

Recovered 5 group3 notes
Fresh searches covered Start Garden 2018 awards, YC S22, the November 2022 seed, Michigan grants, later follow-ons and the 2025 Figma acquisition. Five disclosed events/awards are tabulated, not licensing or acquisition proceeds. Contemporaneous Fox17 July 10, 2018 coverage says all 100 April finalists received $1K and explicitly names Payload/James Mikrut among the later $20K winners; the distinct April $1K and July $20K awards are retained, with medium confidence on the finalist allocation. A later Crain’s caption calls the $20K check the first outside funding, so that shorthand discrepancy is noted rather than silently dropping the earlier contemporaneous award. June 2022 $500K YC investment is explicit in Payload’s own post and dated by June 21 Crain’s coverage. November 2022 $4.7M seed and lead Gradient Ventures come from Payload’s release; Payload’s contemporaneous LinkedIn post adds Rogue Capital and Twenty Two Ventures as participants. YC appears explicitly in both its earlier accelerator event and the seed syndicate; no participant is inferred solely from a cap table. Secondary databases/government regional reporting describe total seed fundraising over $5M, supporting treating the $500K and $4.7M as distinct disclosures, though no unsupported extra cumulative round is added. October 12, 2023 grant was $302,500, not the $875,000 planned capital investment; the MEDC success-story update says the grant was terminated by mutual agreement in October 2026 with no funds disbursed. The grant row is therefore explicitly an awarded, subsequently cancelled commitment, not cash received. Figma’s June 2025 acquisition is excluded, with no ordinary financing inferred from its consideration; Figma’s own IPO is not a Payload funding event. The company describes bootstrapped/moonlit development before fundraising, but that does not exclude the separately reported competition awards. No additional material funding found. ## README

# TRISTAN AI deployment and design simulation with Kenning and Renode

This repository provides resources and tools for simulating embedded RISC-V platforms with a special focus on Machine Learning applications.

## Verification and simulation of TRISTAN IPs

All projects related to the simulation, verification, coverage, and design analysis are found under ./simulation.

To simplify the simulation of RISC-V cores, as well as to enable testing, verification and coverage analysis for RISC-V cores and the surrounding subsystems, the Renode framework can be used.
Renode is a framework for simulating physical hardware systems, including CPUs, peripherals, sensors, and more.
It allows running software in a simulated environment, collecting the required information, and testing both the software and designs.
Renode can be easily co-simulated with Verilog models running in Verilator, Questa, and other.

For the purpose of simulating Verilog/SystemVerilog models, the Verilator framework was expanded within the TRISTAN project.

This repository provides various tools for the simulation, verification and development of Verilog/SystemVerilog modules, with a special focus on RISC-V platforms:

* renode-dpi-examples - provides a sample integration between Renode and Verilog models using SystemVerilog Direct Programming Interface (DPI) calls, supporting both Verilator and Questa simulators.
* renode-systemc-examples - provides the tools for creating Renode simulations using components written in SystemC, as well as integration samples.
* renode-verilator-integration - provides sample Verilog models, and the wrapper code for co-simulation with Renode.
* pyrenode3 - provides Python bindings for Renode, which allow orchestrating and analyzing the emulation from the Python level.
* sv-bugpoint - provides a tool for creating minimal SystemVerilog code from a larger design, based on user-defined property of the scope code.

For more details, follow the co-simulation chapter of the Renode documentation.

Run from a notebook with: await replay()

from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path('/workspace/audit_work')
async def replay(destination=BASE / 'group6_replayed_sources'):
    evidence = json.loads((BASE / 'group6_evidence.json').read_text())

    requests = {}
    for section in ('downloads', 'raw_fetches', 'api_fetches'):

            name = Path(item.get('path', '')).name
            if not name:

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, timeout=90) as client:
        for url, name in requests.items():
            async with client.stream('GET', url) as response:
                response.raise_for_status()
                with (destination / name).open('wb') as handle:
                    async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                        handle.write(chunk)

 async with sem:

apiurl='https://gtr.ukri.org/api/v3/awards'
async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60,follow_redirects=True) as cl:
 results_api=await asyncio.gather(*(cl.get(apiurl,params={'query':q}) for q in ['Hero 2 Product Range','Novel Partial Hand Prosthesis','Digital clinical pathway for upper limb prosthetics','End-to-end digital service for upper limb amputees']))
 ukri_awards=[]
 for rr0 in results_api:
  data=rr0.json()

 details=await asyncio.gather(*(cl.get(a['href']) for a in ukri_awards))

print([(a['projectTitle'],a['startDate'],a['href']) for a in ukri_awards])
for a in ukri_awards:
 d=ukri_details[a['href']]
 print(a['projectTitle'],[(p['organisationName'],p.get('grantOffer')) for p in d.get('participantValues',[])])

USD amounts are blank because disclosed allocations are EUR136850 (AXIOM), EUR470750 (X-MINE), EUR645250 (VEDLIoT), EUR300000 (EXCEED; grant-agreement maximum subject to final confirmation) and EUR788593.75 (TRISTAN), not the much larger consortium totals. Dates are grant signature months: Dec 2014, May 2017, Jul 2020, Oct 2020 and Nov 2022; corresponding project starts were Mar 2015, Jun 2017, Nov 2020, Nov 2020 and Dec 2022. The European Commission is the funding body, not an equity investor; consortium coordinators/partners are not investors. No independently substantiated equity, debt, crowdfunding, token, IPO or secondary funding event was found in this scope. No currency conversion was performed; event-type taxonomy remains provisional because supplied rules were unavailable.

 bela Fresh searches covered Bela/Augmented Instruments equity and grants, both Kickstarter campaigns, Crowd Supply maker profile/current and archived campaigns, and Bela Gem/Gliss updates; four rewards-crowdfunding events were verified. Bela Kickstarter closed Apr 2016 with GBP54902 from 530 backers; Trill closed Oct 2019 with GBP25375 from 412 backers, so both USD cells are blank, without exchange conversion. Archived original Crowd Supply campaign pages verify Gliss USD67951, funded Jan 31 2023 (285 backers), and Bela Gem Stereo and Multi USD64748, funded Jul 31 2025 (330 backers); these are campaign totals, not cumulative venture funding. Individual backer names and round leads are not disclosed, so those fields are blank; Kickstarter and Crowd Supply themselves are not inferred investors. Trill revised sensors were rewards in the Gliss campaign, not a separate new funding round. Academic EPSRC/UKRI and Royal Academy of Engineering awards to the Augmented Instruments Laboratory/Andrew McPherson were not assigned to the company: the research-chair page lists Augmented Instruments Ltd among the academic project's funders rather than proving receipt by the venture. No company equity, debt, token, IPO or secondary financing was substantiated. Event-type taxonomy remains provisional because supplied rules were unavailable.

The 2019 company announcement explicitly states USD3000000, so this is not a currency conversion. The 2020 round is EUR2800000; company and CDTI-derived Jan 2021 coverage describe the SAME 2020 investment, so the Catalonia portal's Jan 2021 EUR2.8m entry is not duplicated. An Oct 2021 follow-on is reported in Nov 2021 coverage; EUR1035000 is CDTI's contribution, not the total round. Event investors are taken from that source (Alma Mundi Fund II, FIDES 4 and Mondragon promotion fund alongside CDTI), not the portal's questionable Euveka attribution. The Mar 2024 report explicitly says the next co-investment closed in FEBRUARY 2024: CDTI contributed EUR315000 alongside Alma Mundi Fund II and Mondragon; no total round is disclosed. The Nov 2024 company release confirms new investment from unnamed established Spanish industrial firms; Catalonia's official startup portal reports EUR3000000 for that event. Those EUR amounts are not converted to USD. The company footer also discloses ICEX Next support co-financed by ERDF; one grant/support row is retained with date and USD amount blank because no award month, year or amount is stated. The 2025 Quantum acquisition, bankruptcy and AstroPrint/Supernova corporate transactions are not counted as outside funding to BCN3D. Mondragon Ventures denotes the corporate promotion venture fund; Clave Capital is its manager, not an extra independently disclosed investor in the same ticket. No other debt, secondary, token, crowdfunding or IPO financing was substantiated. Event-type taxonomy remains provisional because supplied rules were unavailable.

 bitcraze Fresh searches covered investors/funding, Kickstarter and ordinary preorders, Minc incubation, bootstrapping, grants/Vinnova and 2025–2026 updates. Official Vinnova project 2022-01270 names Bitcraze AB as coordinator and discloses SEK317289; USD is blank without conversion. Jul 2022 is project start (project ran through Feb 2024), not a separately disclosed grant-signature month. Minc incubation is retained as an accelerator event because PitchBook explicitly lists Minc as an investor, but no cash amount/equity terms are public: the company blog documents joining in MAR 2014, overriding PitchBook's conflicting Mar 2024 date. This row does not assert a cash investment. Early company comments describe funding the initial batch from founders' pockets; this supports initial self-funding only, not a claim that the venture never received outside funding. WIRED describes ordinary Seeed preorders and the founders deciding against Kickstarter, so those sales were not manufactured into a crowdfunding round. No additional equity, debt, secondary, token or IPO event was substantiated after reasonable searches, including a dedicated Vinnova project search. Event-type taxonomy remains provisional because supplied rules were unavailable.

 open-bionics Searched precursor crowdfunding, Intel/Disney/Techstars awards, prizes, seed/Series A, SBRI/Innovate UK/local grants, 2022–2024 crowdfunding, 2024 NatWest debt and 2025–2026 equity; fetched company/investor/press sources, Crowdcube campaigns, UKRI current award API and Companies House cash-share allotments. Incomplete: source databases disagree materially and several private rounds remain poorly disclosed. October 2013 Open Hand Project precursor campaign reached GBP39000 (later reporting about GBP42000); no unsupported USD conversion. September 2014 Intel $50000 grant is consistent with founder retrospective; November $200000 runner-up prize is separate. Intel Capital January 2015 $100000 convertible is database-only, low confidence. Disney/Techstars $120000 package is a single accelerator event ($20000 acceptance plus optional $100000 convertible note); not counted again as separate July/August grants; uptake/instrument split is not independently confirmed. Dyson UK prize GBP2000, Nominet September 2016 grant amount undisclosed, and SBRI feasibility GBP100000 are retained with blank USD. Feasibility was announced December 2016 in TechCrunch and quantified January 2017 by health network; CSV uses quantified January announcement, not a separate December event. SBRI clinical-trial award GBP697464 has no verified month, so date is blank; aggregator December 2017 grant GBP700000 is treated as the same award, not another round. The 2017 Rewired investment is confirmed in investor’s July launch, despite database dates December 2017/January 2018. August 2017 PitchBook $565000 early-stage transaction is retained at low confidence but may overlap another seed closing. January 2018 GBP435000 seed names Rewired and Social Tech Trust in aventure database, with amount/month corroborated by founder interview. January 2019 Series A USD5.9m comes from TechCrunch; co-leads Foresight Williams, Ananda and Downing and participant Rathbone Nominees come from UK government, while TechCrunch calls only Foresight lead; this role disagreement is disclosed. Uncorroborated August 2019 $35m and $1000 database entries are excluded, not summed. Apparent January 2020 GBP250k grant is not additional: current UKRI records show GBP74992 starting 2020-06 and GBP174717.60 starting 2020-10; also GBP50000 starting 2023-04 and GBP229460.27 starting 2024-04. Dates use current API project starts, not stale indexed month values (one month earlier). Local authority GBP20000 award dated 2022-03-03 is distinct. November 2022 SCVC round GBP2.8m is low-confidence database report; its overlap with December 2022/January 2023 crowdfunding and GBP857666.15 off-platform commitments is unresolved. Crowdcube first campaign reports GBP1514842 and is labelled December 2022, though company public launch was January 2023; this is one campaign, not two. February 2024 distinct campaign GBP1118096 includes GBP250000 off-platform commitments (GBP125000 received at disclosure); no duplicate separate row. NatWest GBP600000 loan is November 2024, not a second 2025 loan when case studies appeared. Four cash allotment tranches close 28 March–2 April 2025 (340251 shares at GBP6.37), 24 April (86118 at GBP6.37), 21 May (21825 at GBP6.37 corrected filing), and 23 July (28580 at GBP6.37); investors unnamed, blank USD, no duplicate PitchBook March 2025 $3.82m aggregate. First tranche date is closing month April. Duplicate July filing not duplicated. Nominal-price December 2023 issue and small June 2026 issue have no demonstrated outside-investor identity and were not assumed outside funding. January 2021 private-round entry and full historic share-issue/employee-option distinctions remain unresolved. Pitch@Palace, Women Who Tech finalist status, royalty-free licensing and noncash awards are not treated as cash funding; Women Who Tech winner was Simprints, not Open Bionics.

Anaconda notes Fresh searches covered Continuum Analytics and Anaconda, seed/venture rounds, DARPA, debt/PPP, strategic investors, secondary transactions and 2025–2026 updates; company announcements, SEC filings, reporting and commercial databases were fetched. INCOMPLETE: unresolved public database histories are not silently treated as confirmed funding. Tracxn additionally reports Jan 2014 USD1500000, Dec 2014 USD3000000 grant, Nov 2015 USD325000, Dec 2015 EvoNexus, Oct 2016 USD500000/ExCapsa Group, Dec 2018 USD17500000 and an undated-month 2012 UCSD event; these lack independent corroboration and may include duplicate or misattributed records, so were not added as established separate events. PitchBook additionally shows Aug 2019 debt, Jul 2021 VC, an undated private secondary and Jan 2022 VC without publicly accessible event amounts/participants; these could not satisfy the event-source test or be reconciled and remain gaps. A General Catalyst biography describes an acquisition by Morningside, but supplies no distinct secondary transaction amount/date; not recast as new capital. The seed row uses first sale Dec 2011 and the final Aug 2012 amendment's USD2250000 sold; the earlier USD550000 notice is not another round. The 2016, 2017 and May 2021 equity dates and exact amounts are SEC first-sale months and amounts sold, not offering ceilings. Morningside Venture Partners is named for the June 2021 filing by CB Insights, not by SEC; investor confidence is therefore medium. Citi and Snowflake stage/lead roles are not inferred. The 2022 USD60000000 is an up-to ceiling; debt classification is corroborated by CB Insights/PitchBook, while BlackRock-managed funds are identified by Anaconda. The 2025 USD150000000 is a disclosed lower threshold (the company says OVER this amount), not an exact total; employee liquidity is part of this financing, not a separately quantified duplicate secondary. PPP uses approved principal, not principal-plus-interest forgiven. Shared method limitation: /workspace/deal_rules.md and /workspace/funders_audit_sample.csv were absent despite workspace/memory checks, so types seed, series_a, series_c, venture, debt, grant, crowdfunding and accelerator are provisional descriptive labels, not verified against the unavailable taxonomy; the requested citation-integrity skill was also unavailable. All USD blanks on other ventures mean undisclosed USD or disclosed non-USD without conversion, not zero.
